data.title: Turn an LLM design brief into bounded parameters
data.summary: A generic prop generator and width 0.4–0.8 m, height 0.3–0.6 m ranges. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: The Python API can inspect and modify Blender data and run tools.

prerequisites: An authorized Claude Code / Codex / existing Studio environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: A generic prop generator and width 0.4–0.8 m, height 0.3–0.6 m ranges.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent parameter contract workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: A generic prop generator and width 0.4–0.8 m, height 0.3–0.6 m ranges. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Inspect the existing generator and define a schema with units, bounds and required fields
Ask the LLM for parameters only; reject unknown keys and out-of-range values deterministically
Run one accepted parameter set through the existing generator and save the input/output identity

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned turn an llm design brief into bounded parameters candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: A negative width is rejected before geometry execution
The accepted values appear unchanged in the output receipt
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: A schema-valid request can still produce an ugly or unsuitable object.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: Separate free-form intent from the validated generator input.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me turn an llm design brief into bounded parameters in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: A generic prop generator and width 0.4–0.8 m, height 0.3–0.6 m ranges. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: A negative width is rejected before geometry execution; The accepted values appear unchanged in the output receipt. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
